lines.text: omni ex parte feliciter; de al-Battānī autem ita iudicavit (l. c. p. 913–14): « Author iste sane
« pro suo saeculo admirandi acuminis, ac in administrandis observationibus exercitatissimus,
« ut apparet ex eo quod Solis motum, captis Aequinoctiorum momentis, penitus instaurasse
« videretur, si longius Ptolemaei vestigiis abcedens, Excentricitatem Solis bisecandam esse vi-
« disset..... (1). Observationes vero eius quas solas habemus, per tot saecula inter Ptolemaeum
« et Regiomontanum lapsa, iure conservari atque inter pretiosissima Uraniae <gr>κειμήλια</gr> reponi
« merentur. Praesertim cum usus eximios praebeant in demonstranda Temporis Annui inae-
« qualitate; uti alia occasione probare satago ». Duobus post annis, monens quosdam Anglicos
mercatores usque ar-Raqqah, ab iis Yarecca vocatam, pervenisse, scribebat (2): « The Lati-
« tude thereof was observed by that Albatāni with great accurateness, about eight hundred
« years since; and therefore I recommend it to all that are curious of such Matters, to en-
« deavour to get some good Observation made at this Place, to determin the Height of the
« Pole there, thereby to decide the Controversie, whether there hath really been any Change
« in the Axis of the Earth, in so long an Interval ». Hortatur postea viatores vel mercatores
illic incolentes ut accurate observent phases eclipsium lunarium in urbibus Baghdād, Aleppo
et Alexandria et hoc modo longitudines ipsarum deprehendant, scientiae astronomicae non
paucum inservientes; « for in and near these Places were made all the Observations whereby
« the Middle Motions of the Sun and the Moon are limited: And I could then pronounce
« in what Proportion the Moon’s Motion does Accelerate; which that it does, I think I can
« demonstrate, and shall (God willing) one day, make it appear to the Publick ». Haec suis
verbis referre placuit, ne error semper hodie repetatur Halley ex Albatenii observationibus
accelerationem saecularem motus lunaris deduxisse (3). Eam quidem clarissimus Anglicus astro-
nomus suspicatus erat, veteres eclipses considerans; at eius quantitatem in scriptis suis non
definivit.
Observationes Albatenianas in studio motus Lunae adhibuit Rich. Dunthorne, A
Letter to the Rev. Mr. Richard Mason, concerning the Acceleration of the Lune (Philo-
sophical Transactions, nr. 492, 1749, p. 162–72). Ait enim p. 163: « Then I compared the four
« well-known Eclipses observed by Albategnius with the Tables, and found the computed
« Places of the Moon in three of them considerably too forward: This, if I could have de-
ciety], London 1693, t. XVIII, nr. 204, p. 913-21. —
Partem eius correctionum in notis p. 56-57 retuli.
In radicibus medii motus Solis pro annis 881-901 Chr.
restaurandis errorem 42″ tantum fecit; maiorem in
radicibus motus longitudinis Lunae. Nam annis 881,
est errore inter −9′ 27″ et −10′ 33″ oscillanti. Nodi
ascendentis motus exacte, omissis secundis.
(1) [Excentricitatem bisecaverat Ptolemaeus in
reliquis planetis (Luna et Mercurio exceptis), circu-
lum quem seriores aequantem vocaverunt adhi-
bendo. — <n>Schiaparelli</n>.]
(2) Some account of the ancient state of the
city of Palmyra, with short remarks upon the
inscriptions found there, in Philosophical Transac-
(3) Rem ita perperam exponit <n>J. C. Houzeau</n>,
Vade Mecum de l’astronome, Bruxelles 1882, p. 539:
« Halley ayant examiné, en 1693, les observations
« de la lune d’Albategnius, crut qu’il serait néces-
« saire, pour les représenter, d’ajouter à l’expression
« de la longitude de l’astre, un terme dépendant du
« carré du temps (London, P Tr. 1693, 193 [sic, l. 913];
« 1695, 174). Cette opinion fut confirmée par Dun-
« thorne (London, P Tr., 1747, 412 [sic!]), et bientôt
« ne laissa pas de doute ». Halley, in priore disser-
tatione, ne verbum quidem de acceleratione lunari
dixerat. — Error iam erat apud La Lande, Astro-
nomie, 1a ed., Paris 1764, t. I, p. 583, § 1163.
